Bug-fix release for **uun**. It fixes the problems reported with v0.1.0 on Ubuntu 24.04. If you're on v0.1.0, upgrading is recommended.

## Fixes

- **uun now exits immediately when you quit.** In v0.1.0 the screen closed on `q`, but the process kept running until background checks (apt, snap, npm, network) finished, often requiring Ctrl+C. Quitting now stops those read-only checks, including helper processes they started, and exits at once. A running package update is never interrupted: quitting is refused until it finishes, since stopping apt or dnf mid-install can damage the system. (#10)
- **The daily EoL refresh timer now works.** Under the systemd *user* manager, two sandbox options in the v0.1.0 unit made root-owned files appear to be owned by `nobody`, so uun's file-ownership safety check refused to run and the refresh failed every day. The unit now uses hardening that works in per-user services (syscall filtering, no new privileges, no namespaces or SUID, private umask), and the ownership check is unchanged. This is verified by a new CI job that enables and runs the timer as a normal user on Ubuntu 24.04. (#10)
- **Clear instructions for enabling the timer.** It's a per-user unit, so run `systemctl --user …` as yourself. `sudo systemctl --user …` fails with `Failed to connect to bus`. The install message and README now say so and cover headless servers (`loginctl enable-linger`). (#10)
- **Clear errors instead of tracebacks** when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME` point at a directory uun can't access, or when a config file has a syntax error. An unreadable config is reported, never silently ignored, so settings like `use_sudo = false` can't be dropped. (#7)

## Upgrading

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
sudo apt install ./uun_0.1.1-1_all.deb            # Ubuntu / Debian / Raspberry Pi OS
sudo dnf install ./uun-0.1.1-1.noarch.rpm         # Fedora / RHEL / Rocky / Alma
sudo zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./uun-0.1.1-1.noarch.rpm   # openSUSE Leap

# as your normal user (no sudo):
systemctl --user daemon-reload                         # pick up the fixed timer unit
systemctl --user enable --now uun-eol-refresh.timer
systemctl --user start uun-eol-refresh.service && uun --report   # optional: refresh now
```

If you installed from source with `install.sh`, re-run it to get the fixed unit.

## Packages

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `uun_0.1.1-1_all.deb` | Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 12 / 13, Raspberry Pi OS bookworm+ (arm64 and armhf) |
| `uun-0.1.1-1.noarch.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL / Rocky / Alma 9 (installs `python3.11`+ automatically), openSUSE Leap 15.6 |
| `uun-0.1.1-py3-none-any.whl`, `uun-0.1.1.tar.gz` | `pipx install` / pip on any Linux with Python ≥ 3.11 |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums for all of the above |

Each package was install-tested in clean environments for every distro listed. The tests ran as an unprivileged user, used live end-of-life data, and removed the package cleanly afterwards. Requirements and limitations are unchanged from v0.1.0: Python ≥ 3.11, and the packages aren't GPG-signed (check them against `SHA256SUMS`).

**Full changes:** https://github.com/nc-intezra/uun/compare/v0.1.0...v0.1.1
